title: The stages of the Exodus
summary: Moses' list of the 41 camps between Rameses and the plains of Moab. The route follows OpenBible.info's top-ranked identification for each camp, which puts Mount Sinai in the south of the peninsula (the traditional route). About a third of the camps have no agreed site. Where OpenBible only says a camp was near the one before, the camp is spaced along the line of travel and marked ≈. Legs are straight lines between camps unless the coastline forces a detour.

sources.note: The itinerary itself, camp by camp.
Links Moserah, Bene-jaakan, Gudgodah and Jotbathah, and puts Aaron's death at Moserah.

sources.title: OpenBible.info Bible Geocoding Data
sources.note: Proposed sites and their ranking, weighed across 70+ atlases and commentaries.

via.basis: After the sea crossing the line runs through Uyun Musa (the 'Springs of Moses', in OpenBible's modern-site list) and down the eastern shore of the Gulf of Suez, the natural corridor to Marah. Only the camps are named in the text; the path between them is an estimate.

estimate.basis: The text says only 'by the Red Sea', and OpenBible's point is the middle of the Gulf of Suez. The camp is placed on the gulf's eastern shore near Abu Zenima, between Elim and the Desert of Sin.

OpenBible ranks Sharma in north-west Arabia first, a site that fits the Midian-Sinai theory, not the southern route used for the rest of this map. Kuntilet el-Jerafi is used instead: it has the most votes in OpenBible (100 against Sharma's 40) and lies between Libnah and Kehelathah.
Unidentified. OpenBible's top entry only puts it within 50 km of Haradah. Jebel Araif en-Naqah, its next proposal, lies between Kehelathah and Haradah.
Unidentified. OpenBible only puts it within 50 km of Terah. Tahath, Terah and Mithkah are spaced evenly along the line from Makheloth to Hashmonah.
Unidentified. OpenBible only puts it within 50 km of Mithkah. Tahath, Terah and Mithkah are spaced evenly along the line from Makheloth to Hashmonah.
Unidentified. OpenBible only puts it within 50 km of Hashmonah. Tahath, Terah and Mithkah are spaced evenly along the line from Makheloth to Hashmonah.

via.basis: Jotbathah (Taba) and Abronah (Elath, by Aqaba) are on opposite sides of the Gulf of Aqaba. The line goes around the northern tip of the gulf instead of across the water. Only the camps are named in the text; the path is an estimate.

Back around the northern tip of the Gulf of Aqaba and down its western shore. OpenBible's top site, Jezirat Faraun (Coral Island), lies a few hundred metres offshore, so the last short hop is over water.
Starts from the shore opposite Jezirat Faraun, since the island is offshore. Beyond that the line is straight: the text names no stops between Ezion-geber and Kadesh.

title: The borders of Canaan
summary: The boundary God gives Moses for the land, traced clockwise from the southern tip of the Salt Sea: west across the Negev to the Brook of Egypt, up the Mediterranean coast, east through Lebo-hamath to Hazar-enan, and back down past the Sea of Galilee and the Jordan. Named points use OpenBible.info's top-ranked identification. Where the text names a feature (the Brook, the coast, the Jordan, the Salt Sea), the line follows it. Where a point is unidentified, it is spaced between its neighbours and marked ≈. The northern points are the most debated.

sources.note: Judah's southern border repeats the same line: Akrabbim, Zin, Kadesh-barnea, Hezron/Addar, Azmon, the Brook of Egypt.
Ezekiel's ideal borders repeat the northern and eastern line: Lebo-hamath, Zedad, Hazar-enan, the Jordan.

sources.title: OpenBible.info Bible Geocoding Data
sources.note: Proposed sites and their ranking; courses of Wadi el-Arish and the Jordan (traced from OpenStreetMap, ODbL).

sources.title: Natural Earth 1:10m coastline and lakes
sources.note: The Mediterranean coast and the outline of the Salt Sea.

estimate.basis: 'The end of the Salt Sea' is taken as its southern tip, the southern end of the Dead Sea's southern basin in the Natural Earth outline. OpenBible's point for the Salt Sea is the middle of the lake.

No site identified. OpenBible gives only the Wilderness of Zin as a whole, whose point lies back to the east. Placed midway between the Ascent of Akrabbim and Kadesh-barnea, the points named either side.
The border passes 'south of Kadesh-barnea', so the line is drawn about 4 km south of Ain el-Qudeirat, OpenBible's site for Kadesh.
Where the line from Azmon meets Wadi el-Arish, OpenBible's leading identification of the Brook of Egypt: the upstream end of OpenBible's geometry for it, which is traced from OpenStreetMap.

stations.name: The Sea, at the mouth of the Brook

via.basis: Follows the course of Wadi el-Arish down to the Mediterranean at El-Arish, using OpenBible's geometry for it, which is traced from OpenStreetMap.

estimate.basis: The western border is the coastline itself, traced from the Natural Earth coastline. It is drawn as far north as the northern border's starting point, which the text does not name. That point is taken as the coast due west of Mount Hor.
Unidentified. OpenBible only puts it within 100 km of Riblah. Placed midway between Hazar-enan and Riblah, the points named either side.

stations.name: Slopes east of the Sea of Chinnereth

estimate.basis: The border runs along 'the slopes east of the Sea of Chinnereth' (Galilee), so the line keeps to the rising ground a few kilometres east of its shore.

via.basis: Down the eastern slopes above the Sea of Galilee, a few kilometres inland of the shore.

stations.name: Salt Sea, at the Jordan's mouth

estimate.basis: Where the Jordan enters the Salt Sea: the end of OpenBible's geometry for the Jordan, which is traced from OpenStreetMap.

via.basis: Follows the Jordan from the Sea of Galilee down to the Salt Sea, using OpenBible's geometry for the Jordan, which is traced from OpenStreetMap.

estimate.basis: The Salt Sea itself is the boundary from the Jordan back to its southern tip, where the southern border began, so the line closes down the length of the lake.
